tonight.headline: Waivers clear at 01:00 and you are filing nothing. That is the decision, not an omission.
body: All 118 available players in this league are on waivers, and priority here never resets. You sit 3rd of 10. One claim — any claim, for anyone — drops you to 10th for the remaining fifteen weeks. The best thing on the board is the Jaguars defence at 7.1 against the Ravens' 6.0. That is roughly a point, for a chip you cannot get back.

So the two things worth doing tonight cost nothing. Swap Hockenson in for Loveland, which is free because you already own both. And re-send the Stafford offer to Sack Steel Boys before 01:00, because the same waiver run that you are sitting out is what closes that window: they hold priority 7, and seven startable quarterbacks clear at the same moment.

case.label: What the priority is being saved for
case.body: Saquon Barkley took a stinger on his first carry against Tennessee, missed the first half, and came back wearing a neck roll. Schefter's read on 21 September was that it 'did not sound like a major injury'; RotoWire on 22 September says he could play if symptoms subside. No MRI result has been published. If that turns into a multi-week absence, priority 3 is exactly what you want in hand, and it is the one branch that justifies spending it.

case.label: Why 48% is not the real problem
case.body: JuiceJam project 123.0 to your 118.8. The gap is Jahmyr Gibbs at 25.4 and Kenneth Walker at 21.1, and you are not going to out-run that. You are 0-2 and last in the league in points scored at 183.26, which STRATEGY section 1 says to read as the honest measure rather than the record.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Philadelphia rule Barkley out for multiple weeks before 07:00Z, or Jonathan Taylor or Garrett Wilson goes down in the next eight hours. Any of those and the priority should be spent tonight without hesitation, because that is precisely the need it was held against. Closes wrong if a player somebody else claims this Wednesday becomes a Bloodsports-quality starter inside three weeks.

doFirst.title: Re-send the Stafford offer to Sack Steel Boys tonight
doFirst.subtitle: Their quarterback slot projects 0.0 and both their quarterbacks are hurt. At 01:00 they can fix it for free from the wire and this offer dies.

case.label: Why the clock is real
case.body: This is not urgency for its own sake. Sack Steel Boys hold waiver priority 7, and Bo Nix, Tyler Shough, Kyler Murray, Jordan Love, Bryce Young, C.J. Stroud and Sam Darnold all clear at 07:00Z. The moment any one of those lands, Stafford is worth nothing to them. That is the written falsification clause on this thesis and it fires in eight hours.

case.label: How desperate they actually are
case.body: Verified against tonight's file, not carried forward. Caleb Williams sits in their slot 0 at 0.0 — Ben Johnson said Monday he will not practice this week. Jayden Daniels sits at slot 20 at 0.0 with an elbow dislocation, his second in two years, and roughly a month of recovery reported. Those are the only two quarterbacks on their roster.

case.label: The slot check
case.body: Christian Watson is slot 20 — their bench — so their starting lineup is untouched. One honest caveat carried from this morning: their lineup is stale, and with Puka Nacua unavailable Watson was closer to their de facto starter than the slot column suggested. That has eased today. Nacua is QUESTIONABLE rather than OUT in tonight's file and Sean McVay said he is 'hopeful that he'll play', which makes Watson depth again and makes them likelier to part with him than they were this morning.

case.label: What Watson actually is, corrected upward
case.body: Not depth. Green Bay's leading receiver by usage: 19 targets to Matthew Golden's 18 across two games, and in Week 2 he out-snapped Golden 46 to 42, out-ran him 30 routes to 29 and out-targeted him 11 to 6. He has 188 yards and three touchdowns. He is not on Green Bay's Week 3 injury report, which published Monday because they play Thursday. Jayden Reed is on it — did not practice, neck — which concentrates the targets further.

case.label: The thing to know before you send it
case.body: You already own Matthew Golden. Watson and Golden are the same two-man receiver room on a Green Bay offence that ran 50 plays in Week 2, so acquiring Watson concentrates two of your starting slots into one team and one Thursday game. If that bothers you, ask for George Kittle instead: also slot 20, priced at +2.8 you and +14.4 them weekly and +34.7 and +25.9 on the season, 4 for 4 for 80 and a touchdown in Week 2 on a 29% target-per-route rate, on a managed Achilles workload of about 47% of snaps with Brock Purdy throwing. Kittle solves your tight end slot permanently; Watson is the better season asset. Either is a yes.

case.label: What is genuinely new since 07:15
case.body: Two things, and only two, because re-upgrading an offer on no new information is how this row flip-flopped on Sunday. First, Cheesehead TV's Week 2 snap counts show Watson out-snapped Golden 46-42, out-routed him 30-29 and out-targeted him 11-6 — he is Green Bay's WR1 by usage, which the EVEN downgrade got wrong. Second, Jayden Reed did not practise Monday with a neck injury, so that room is down to two.

case.label: The price, both ways
case.body: You give Matthew Stafford, who has never entered this lineup and cannot while Trevor Lawrence is healthy. Weekly this is +2.5 for you and +13.3 for them. On season projections it is +37.1 you and +21.5 them. Both units agree in both directions, which is the standing rule this roster adopted after the James Cook proposal priced positive weekly and minus 79.8 for the other side on the season.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Sack Steel Boys claim any of those seven quarterbacks at 07:00Z, which closes the window entirely. Or Trevor Lawrence is injured before the trade lands, at which point Stafford is not surplus and the offer must be pulled. Green Bay also play Thursday, so if it lands after Thursday evening you have bought Watson for Week 4 onward, not this week.

doFirst.title: Start T.J. Hockenson over Colston Loveland
doFirst.subtitle: Third consecutive brief with this card. Loveland is still slot 6 and Hockenson still slot 20 in the 21:52 file. It costs nothing — you own both.

case.label: Chicago's quarterback room, which is the whole card
case.body: Caleb Williams strained his right hamstring in the fourth quarter against Minnesota; Ben Johnson confirmed Monday he will not practice this week. Tyson Bagent, the backup who was supposed to replace him, entered the concussion protocol — Rapoport, 22 September. Case Keenum is in line to start, and he has not played a regular-season game since December 2023. The emergency option is an undrafted rookie on the practice squad.

case.label: Loveland was already failing with a real quarterback
case.body: Five targets across two games, one catch for three yards. His route participation fell from 89.5% to 76.3% while his pass-blocking snaps rose from 5.3% to 15.8% — Chicago are using him to block. His average separation collapsed from 3.7 yards last season to 2.1. That is a role moving the wrong way before the quarterback got worse.

case.label: The matchup on top of it
case.body: Philadelphia have allowed three fantasy points to tight ends all season, 3rd-stingiest in the league. Tampa Bay, where Hockenson plays, have allowed the 4th-most, 29th of 32.

case.label: Why Hockenson and not simply 'the other one'
case.body: Kyler Murray cleared concussion protocol and was confirmed by Kevin O'Connell on Monday as Minnesota's Week 3 starter. Hockenson ran 19 routes in Week 2 against Josh Oliver's 4 — he is unambiguously the receiving tight end, not a rotational piece. The 69.2% snap share is a role, not a projection.

case.label: The arithmetic that cuts against me
case.body: Recorded because it should be. ESPN still prices Loveland at 9.9 and Hockenson at 9.2, so this swap makes your projection 0.7 points worse on the number. And the Murray half of the case is an inference rather than evidence: Hockenson has nine targets in two games, Murray has thrown five passes all season, and DK Network's piece on Murray's return names Justin Jefferson as the beneficiary and gives no tight end usage at all. What is not an inference is Loveland: one catch for three yards behind a quarterback room that has lost two men.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Chicago target Loveland six or more times against Philadelphia while Hockenson stays under four in a low-dropback Vikings game. Minnesota won 9-3 in Week 2 on 24 dropbacks in the rain, so the low-volume Hockenson is a genuine risk and not a hypothetical one. Either result says I reacted to two games.

whatWentWrong.title: The Hockenson swap has now been written three times and made zero times
whatWentWrong.lead: It was a ghost card on 20 September, a live card on 21 September, a live card this morning, and Loveland is still in your starting lineup tonight.

case.label: What it has cost so far
case.body: Nothing yet, because Chicago play Monday and Minnesota play Sunday — neither game has happened. But the cost of the pattern is that a free, reversible, no-priority lineup change is the single easiest thing on this brief and it is the one that keeps not happening.

case.label: Why it is not churn to repeat it
case.body: STRATEGY section 3 closes a slot that has changed hands in seven days. This slot has not changed hands — the card has never been executed. Repeating an unexecuted recommendation is not the same as re-litigating a made decision.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Chicago naming Caleb Williams active on Saturday, which would restore the premise. Nothing else.

whatWentWrong.title: Chicago's quarterback room got worse today, not better
whatWentWrong.lead: The backup who was going to throw to Loveland is now in concussion protocol himself.

case.label: What changed since this morning
case.body: At 07:15 the read was that Tyson Bagent would start and that this was already a downgrade. Rapoport reported on 22 September that Bagent is in the concussion protocol. Case Keenum, last regular-season appearance December 2023, is in line to start against a Philadelphia defence allowing three fantasy points to tight ends all year.

case.label: The source conflict, stated rather than smoothed
case.body: RotoWire's Week 3 injury column, also dated 22 September, still lists Bagent as the likely starter. It was written before the concussion news broke the same day. No outlet has formally confirmed Keenum — every one says 'in line to' or 'could'. I am taking the newer report.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Bagent clears protocol by Saturday, or Williams practices Friday. Either puts a competent passer back in front of Loveland and the swap above becomes a coin flip rather than a clear call.

whatWentWrong.title: The Watson offer has been sitting unanswered since yesterday and it expires at 01:00 tonight
whatWentWrong.lead: Not because of a rule, but because the waiver run you are sitting out is the thing that solves their problem for free.

case.label: The mechanism
case.body: Sack Steel Boys hold priority 7 and seven startable quarterbacks clear at 07:00Z. Their motivation to pay a real receiver for Matthew Stafford exists only while their starting slot projects 0.0. After 01:00 it probably does not.

case.label: What was lost by waiting
case.body: Nothing yet. But this offer was downgraded from LIKELY to EVEN on Sunday and re-upgraded this morning, and across that time it has never been sent. The window was always going to close at a waiver run; it is closing at this one.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Green Bay play Thursday. If the trade lands after Thursday evening you have bought Watson for Week 4 onward rather than this week, which is still worth doing but is a different trade.

whatWentWrong.title: Rashee Rice is the fourth-most-targeted player on his own team and you are starting him
whatWentWrong.lead: The watch row opened on 19 September has resolved, and it resolved against him.

case.label: The clause and the outcome
case.body: The condition was 'a second week under a 15% target share.' Week 1: two targets on 27 Mahomes attempts, 7.4%. Week 2: six of 47, 12.8%, with Travis Kelce out-targeting him 11 to 6. Two weeks, both under 15. The clause fired.

case.label: The number that hurts most
case.body: SI on 22 September has him fourth on Kansas City in targets and receptions — behind Kelce, Xavier Worthy and Kenneth Walker III, with Tyquan Thornton two behind him. Week 2 snap counts have Worthy at 86% and Rice at 79%. Kansas City are 11.5-point favourites at Miami, which is the game script that takes the ball out of the air late.

case.label: Why this connects to the trade above
case.body: Because it is the argument for acquiring Watson rather than waiting. Your receiver room is thinner than its projections say: Rice at an 11% two-game share, Golden now second in usage on his own team behind the man you are trying to acquire. The wire cannot fix that without spending priority. A trade can.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A normal Week 3 line at Miami closes this row and says the first two weeks were game script. I could not verify the slot-rate half of the original thesis — the claim that he fell from 40%+ to 25% — from any September 2026 source, so that part stays unproven.

trades.copyText: Hi — you're starting a QB projecting 0.0 with Caleb Williams not practising and Daniels out about a month. I'll send you Matthew Stafford for Christian Watson. Straight up. It's a bigger gain for you than for me on this week's numbers — you're filling a ~15-point hole at QB and giving up a bench receiver — but Stafford can't crack my lineup behind Lawrence, so it's the one deal that works for both of us. Say the word before waivers clear tonight.

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +1.6 this week and +22.2 across the season — smaller than yours weekly, larger than it looks on the season, and both are stated here rather than hidden.

youGet.name: Lamar Jackson
youGet.detail: QB BAL · 20.1 wk · 297.3 szn · their slot 20

case.label: The structural surplus
case.body: Re-verified on tonight's file: Lamar Jackson sits at slot 20 behind Josh Allen at slot 0 in a one-quarterback league. He scores Team 13 exactly zero every week. This is the surplus STRATEGY section 7 says to trade into.

case.label: What they get that they can use
case.body: Their running backs behind Christian McCaffrey are Rachaad White at 9.4 weekly and 144.7 on the season, and Blake Corum at 8.6 on their bench. Tuten at 11.0 and 166.9 walks into a slot they actually start. He has 131 rushing yards to Chris Rodriguez's 36 across two games and took the Week 2 one-yard touchdown, so he owns the goal line, and Travis Etienne signed with New Orleans, so the Jacksonville backfield is genuinely his rather than a committee.

case.label: Why it is a longshot anyway
case.body: Name value. Managers do not trade Lamar Jackson for a rookie back, whatever the lineup math says, and this has now been standing for three days without a reply. I am publishing it at honest odds rather than dressing it up.

case.label: Send one Team 13 offer, never both
case.body: The Garrett Wilson offer below goes to the same manager. Sending both signals you are shopping and invites them to counter on the cheaper one.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Josh Allen gets hurt, at which point Lamar becomes their starter and this closes instantly. Or Rico Dowdle's toe keeps him out and Team 13 decide Rachaad White is fine anyway, removing their running back need. Or Lamar appears on a Baltimore injury report — he is not on one, checked tonight against two 2026-dated sources. Or Saquon Barkley is ruled out, which makes Tuten your starter and the offer must be pulled before it is accepted. Expect a counter asking for Jonathan Taylor; that is the answer no.

He'd start for you immediately over Rachaad White — Tuten prices out about 22 points ahead of White across the rest of the season. It's a bigger weekly gain for me than for you and I'm not going to pretend otherwise; the reason it works for you is that it turns a dead roster spot into a starter.

case.label: Why this is ranked last
case.body: It asks for a slot 0 player — their starting quarterback — while the Lamar offer asks for a bench body. Four tenths of a point a week is not a reason for anyone to move a starter.

case.label: The only version that works

The read that makes it thinkable at all is the opposite one: 88% route participation but only a 21% target share, with Adonai Mitchell leading the Jets in Week 2 at 32% and a 28% per-route rate. If you believe Wilson is the third option on his own team's target tree, selling at full name value for an elite quarterback is defensible. I do not believe it yet on one week.

worthALook.name: Rashod Bateman
worthALook.lead: Declined here for a fifth straight run, and tonight the evidence finally moved my way.

case.label: Why he was ever interesting
case.body: Nine targets and 7 for 88 with a score at New Orleans while Zay Flowers sat, with Ja'Kobi Lane and Devontez Walker also out, and an 8.02 ownership jump in a day.

case.label: Why he is not worth priority here
case.body: He is on waivers and priority in this league never resets. Section 6 permits spending it only on a player who starts immediately or a genuine league-winner. One nine-target game with two team-mates hurt is neither, and he would sit behind Wilson, Rice and Golden.

case.label: The number that settled it tonight
case.body: His ownership change is now minus 0.12 and his band has fallen from MONEY to OWNED. The market that was buying him on Saturday has stopped. I claimed him in Chem on Saturday, where priority is free, and I am pulling that card tonight too.

case.label: When to act
case.body: If he clears waivers unclaimed tomorrow he becomes a free agent and costs nothing at all, at which point he is a free add against MarShawn Lloyd's seat. Promotion to a card requires both Flowers ruled out again and an injury to Rice or Golden — not either alone.

worthALook.name: Zach Charbonnet
worthALook.lead: You dropped him on 18 September. He is still OUT and still not worth a claim.

case.label: Why he is on this list at all
case.body: Recorded so a familiar name reappearing on the wire is not mistaken for a discovery. He left this roster at 16:29 on 18 September and entered the wire on waivers.

case.label: The status, checked tonight
case.body: Still carrying an OUT designation in the 21:52 file, with a 0.0 weekly projection and no analyst rank. The 139.4 season projection is what makes him look claimable; the OUT tag is what he actually is.

case.label: Why waiting beats claiming in every branch
case.body: Spending never-resetting priority on a running back who cannot play this week is the clearest possible misuse of it. If Seattle publish a dated return he becomes a free agent again and can be re-added for nothing. The only cost of waiting is another manager claiming an OUT back, which nobody in this league has done all season.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Seattle publishing a return date, and Charbonnet reaching genuine free agency rather than waivers. Both, not either.

doNotChase.name: Rico Dowdle
doNotChase.lead: The top running back on this wire by season projection, and he is hurt.

case.label: Why he looks like the play
case.body: 85.0% rostered nationally and available here, a 152.1 season projection — the highest of any available back — and the OWNED band that STRATEGY section 4 calls the strongest wire signal in a shallow league.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: He left Week 2 with a toe injury and was ruled out, having managed nine touches to Jaylen Warren's thirteen before he exited. It is the second time he has exited with that toe, so it is recurring rather than a one-off, and he is day-to-day. He also carries a QUESTIONABLE tag in tonight's file.

case.label: And the seat is wrong anyway
case.body: Claiming a day-to-day backup back would spend never-resetting priority on a player who is behind Pittsburgh's listed RB1. That is the exact opposite of the bar in section 6.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Pittsburgh clearing him for Week 3 and Warren appearing on an injury report, together. Warren is not on one.

doNotChase.name: Omarion Hampton
doNotChase.lead: The solver's best-priced trade in either league tonight, and it must not be sent.

case.label: What the numbers say
case.body: Matthew Stafford for Omarion Hampton prices at +3.5 you and +12.3 them weekly, and +50.7 you against +7.9 them on the season. It passes the both-sides-gain gate on both units, which is normally enough.

case.label: The number that kills the case
case.body: Hampton is slot 2. That is their starting running back, projecting 15.1 this week and 219.0 on the season. The runbook's standing rule is to check the slot column before naming anyone in a trade, because a run once described a team's starting quarterback as a player who never plays and shipped it twice.

case.label: Why the number lies here
case.body: Their +12.3 weekly gain is an artefact of their quarterback slot sitting at 0.0. Any quarterback appears to fill a fifteen-point hole. It makes every Stafford offer look enormous for them regardless of what comes back, which is why Watson — a bench player — is the version that gets sent and Hampton is the version that gets recorded here.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Nothing about this specific trade. The record exists so the next run does not rediscover it as the best-priced offer on the board and send it.

doNotChase.name: Jaguars D/ST
doNotChase.lead: The required defence comparison. Better than what you have, and still not worth it here.

case.label: The comparison, reported rather than omitted
case.body: Best available on this wire: Vikings 7.5, Jaguars 7.1, Bengals 6.7, Browns 6.4. You start Baltimore at 6.0, in the highest-total game of the week at 52.5 with Dallas implied at 25. Draft Sharks rank Jacksonville 6th, Minnesota 4th and Baltimore 25th. The upgrade is real and it is worth roughly 1.1 to 1.5 points.

case.label: Why it does not happen
case.body: Every player on this wire is on waivers and priority here never resets. Spending a season-long chip from 3rd of 10 on a one-week defensive stream is the single clearest violation of section 6 available tonight. This has been the standing answer since 16 September and it has not moved.

case.label: The cost, named rather than hidden
case.body: You are knowingly starting the worst-situated defence on your board and eating about a point and a half. In Chem, where priority resets weekly, I claimed Minnesota tonight for exactly this reason. The two leagues get opposite answers on identical evidence, and that asymmetry is the whole point of reading the waiver setting live.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A defence reaching genuine free agency in this league rather than waivers, at which point the stream is costless and happens the same hour. Nothing on tonight's board qualifies — all 118 entries are on waivers.

doNotChase.name: Eddy Pineiro
doNotChase.lead: The required kicker comparison, and the answer is hold Jason Myers for a seventh run.

case.label: The comparison
case.body: Best available by ESPN projection on this wire: Pineiro 9.8, Trey Smack 9.1, Daniel Carlson 8.7, Cam Little and Chase McLaughlin 8.4. Myers is 9.4. Pineiro is +0.4. Draft Sharks have Myers 9th this week at 8.4 against Seattle at Washington.

case.label: Why it is not close
case.body: Four tenths of a point, for a waiver priority that never resets, from 3rd of 10. STRATEGY forbids moves worth under a point outright and names fractional streams specifically. Pineiro is also 79.6% rostered, so he is the one kicker on this board somebody else might actually claim.

case.label: The churn note
case.body: This seat changed hands on 18 September when Cam Little went out for Myers, and again the day before that. The seven-day window expires on 25 September. Even if the gap were worth having, moving it a third time inside a week is the pattern section 3 exists to stop.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Myers finishing outside the top twenty in Week 3 while a top-five kicker reaches genuine free agency here. As a free agent, never as a claim.

settled.title: Read the existing daily file before overwriting it (standing rule, 22 September)
settled.result: Broken by me this run and caught before publishing. I read this morning's two briefs for their section counts and card titles rather than their contents, and nearly dropped the George Kittle fallback, the Golden-plus-Watson stacking risk and the honest 'Murray upgrade is an inference' caveat — all of which the 07:15 run had researched properly. All three are restored above. Reading a file's shape is not reading the file.

settled.title: Spend no waiver priority before Wednesday 07:00Z (this morning)
settled.result: Held, and re-tested against tonight's evidence rather than carried. The clause was 'unless Barkley is ruled out for a multi-week absence, or Taylor or Wilson goes down.' Barkley is not ruled out — Schefter called it not major, RotoWire says he could play, no MRI result has been published, and Philadelphia play Monday. Taylor is off the Colts' Week 3 report entirely. Nothing fired.

settled.title: Rashee Rice is an untouchable starter (16-19 September, five runs)
settled.result: Broken. The watch row opened on 19 September required a second week under a 15% target share. Week 1 was 7.4%, Week 2 was 12.8%. He is fourth on his own team in targets. He still starts this week — there is nothing better — but he is now a sell-high candidate rather than a fixture.

settled.title: Downgrade the Stafford-for-Watson offer to EVEN on their capacity to pay (21 September)
settled.result: Wrong, and reversed for the second time. The downgrade reasoned that Watson was Sack Steel Boys' injury cover for Puka Nacua. What it missed is that their quarterback slot projects 0.0 on both bodies, which is a larger hole than a questionable tag. Back at LIKELY, and it should have been sent on Sunday.

settled.title: Hold MarShawn Lloyd rather than drop him (19 September)
settled.result: Held, with half the clause fired. The condition is 'Brooks or Kaleb Johnson out-touches Lloyd in two consecutive weeks.' Week 2 was one such week — Brooks 27 snaps to Lloyd's 16, Johnson leading the team in carries. Green Bay play Thursday, so Week 3 settles it. Josh Jacobs remains on the Commissioner's Exempt List.

settled.title: Keep Matthew Golden in the flex over Devaughn Vele (21 September)
settled.result: Held, and it is closer than it was. Vele played 96% of New Orleans' snaps in Week 2, the highest on the team and ahead of Chris Olave at 84%, on roughly a 20% target share. Golden fell behind Christian Watson in Green Bay's Week 2 usage, 6 targets to 11. ESPN prices them 11.4 to 11.6 — two tenths apart, which is below the floor STRATEGY sets for making a move. Reported as a decision rather than an omission.

settled.title: Hold Jason Myers at kicker (18 September, seven runs)
settled.result: Held. Best available upgrade is four tenths of a point for a priority that never resets, and the seat is still inside its seven-day churn window until 25 September.

settled.title: Never spend IPADE waiver priority on a defence (16 September, every run)
settled.result: Held, and it cost about a point and a half tonight. Minnesota at 7.5 and Jacksonville at 7.1 both beat Baltimore's 6.0. In Chem, where priority resets weekly, the same evidence produced a claim. Opposite answers on identical evidence is the correct output here.

settled.title: Do not send Hockenson for James Cook to Metcalf Gala (this morning)
settled.result: Held, and the reason strengthened. Dallas Goedert's sprained MCL is now reported as several weeks rather than one, so their tight-end hole is real — but the trade still prices at minus 79.8 for them on the season because Cook is 253.2 and his replacement is 173.4. The standing rule stands: no trade published unless weekly and season pricing agree.

settled.title: Check the other team's slot column before naming anyone in a trade (standing rule)
settled.result: Earned its keep tonight. The solver's best-priced offer in either league was Stafford for Omarion Hampton at +50.7 season for you — and Hampton is Sack Steel Boys' slot 2 starting running back. Recorded in Do Not Chase above so the next run does not find it and send it.

settled.title: Report season-long value as unavailable, per the runbook's limitations (standing)
settled.result: Overturned, and it turns out this was already settled. A closed decision-log entry from 21 September (chem-seasonproj-live-2026-09-21) found seasonProj recomputes after each slate, yet this morning's brief still carried the 'unavailable' line. Tonight's snapshots corroborate the closed entry: Isaiah Likely's weekly number moved 11.7 to 12.3 between the 12:52 and 21:52 files today, and Bhayshul Tuten's season projection moved 162.5 on 21 September to 166.9 tonight. The runbook's own liveness test is whether two snapshots days apart are identical. They are not. The standing line should have been retired yesterday.

settled.title: Read settings.scoring and the flex slot live every run (Step 2, standing)
settled.result: Read tonight. IPADE is full PPR, scoring 1, flex slot 23 takes RB, WR and TE, waiver priority never resets. Fourteen scoring items differ from Chem, so no projection crossed between the two briefs.

settled.title: Cross-check every source against its date (20 September, standing rule)
settled.result: Caught two traps tonight. An SI piece headlined 'Eagles fans get good news on Saquon Barkley' — also a stinger, also a Tuesday — is dated 17 December 2025. Two Brock Purdy 'will sit Week 3' stories are from September 2025. None was used.

cannotSee.label: Saquon Barkley's MRI result
cannotSee.body: It is the single most consequential unknown in this brief and no September 2026 source has published it. Philadelphia were off Monday and play Monday night, so their first real practice report lands later this week — after waivers have already processed. The decision to hold priority is being made without it.

cannotSee.label: Wednesday's injury reports
cannotSee.body: Only Atlanta and Green Bay have Week 3 practice reports, because they play Thursday. Every other team's first report lands Wednesday, after the 01:00 waiver run. Everything decided tonight is decided one day early.

cannotSee.label: Rivals' pending claims
cannotSee.body: ESPN never returns another manager's pending claims, and this file carries no pending-claim field at all — not even yours. Whether Sack Steel Boys have already filed on a quarterback from priority 7 is invisible, and it is the thing that closes the Watson window.

cannotSee.label: Whether Case Keenum actually starts for Chicago
cannotSee.body: Every source says 'in line to' or 'could'. None has formally confirmed it, and RotoWire's own Week 3 injury column published the same day still lists Tyson Bagent, having been written before the concussion news broke. The Hockenson swap does not depend on which of the two it is, but the size of the edge does.

cannotSee.label: Rashee Rice's slot rate
cannotSee.body: The original watch row rested on a fall from a 40%-plus slot rate to 25%. No September 2026 source I could reach publishes his slot splits — Arrowhead Pride's snap-count analysis is blocked to fetching. The target-share half is verified from three independent sources; the slot half is not, and I am not treating it as established.

cannotSee.label: Which source is right about the Chiefs' receiver hierarchy
cannotSee.body: SI says Rice has the most passing snaps on the roster. AtoZ Sports' Week 2 counts have Worthy at 86% and Rice at 79%. RotoWire has Rice at 55% and calls him the number one receiver. Three sources, three answers. I used the raw snap counts.

cannotSee.label: Week 2's fantasy scores
cannotSee.body: The file carries only the current scoring period, so every actual is null and Week 2's results are gone from it. The settled list above is reconstructed from the decision log and from reporting, not from the file.

cannotSee.label: MarShawn Lloyd's Week 3 role
cannotSee.body: Green Bay play Thursday and have published an injury report he is not on, but nothing tells me whether Chris Brooks out-snaps him again. His hold clause needs a second consecutive week and Thursday is when it resolves — which is before the next waiver run but after tonight.

cannotSee.label: How much the matchup grades are worth
cannotSee.body: Every grade above is a two-game sample from footballdb's 2026 points-allowed table, and that table is standard scoring rather than PPR. At n=2 a single blowout moves a defence ten places. They break ties; they do not decide anything on this roster.

cannotSee.body: Built from the 21:52 UTC snapshot, 16:52 Mexico City. Nothing in it updates. The waiver deadline it is written around is eight hours after it was written, and the next brief lands after that deadline has passed.
